results.summary: A group $G$ is right-orderable when it admits a linear order $\le$ that is invariant under right multiplication: $a \le b$ implies $ac \le bc$ for all $a, b, c \in G$.

results.title: Even pseudoprime
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A natural number $N$ is an even pseudoprime if $N$ is even, $N > 2$ and $2^N \equiv 2 \pmod{N}$.

results.title: The set of even pseudoprimes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The set of even pseudoprimes is the set of natural numbers $N$ such that $N$ is even, $N > 2$ and $2^N \equiv 2 \pmod{N}$.

results.title: Even pseudoprimes are even
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every even pseudoprime $N$ is an even natural number.

results.title: Even pseudoprimes exceed two
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every even pseudoprime $N$ satisfies $N > 2$.

results.title: Fermat congruence for even pseudoprimes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $N$ is an even pseudoprime, then $2^N \equiv 2 \pmod{N}$.

results.title: Even pseudoprimes are not prime
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: No even pseudoprime is a prime number: the only even prime is $2$, and every even pseudoprime is greater than $2$.

results.title: Odd prime divisors of an even pseudoprime
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N$ be an even pseudoprime and $p$ an odd prime dividing $N$, and write $\ell_2(p)$ for the multiplicative order of $2$ modulo $p$. Then $N \equiv p \pmod{p\,\ell_2(p)}$, $\ell_2(p)$ is odd, $p \equiv 1$ or $7 \pmod 8$, and $14p \le N$.

results.title: Even pseudoprimes modulo 16
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every even pseudoprime $N$ satisfies $N \equiv 2 \pmod{16}$ or $N \equiv 14 \pmod{16}$.

results.title: Square prime factors of even pseudoprimes are Wieferich primes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N$ be an even pseudoprime and $p$ a prime with $p^2 \mid N$. Then $p$ is a Wieferich prime, that is $2^{p-1} \equiv 1 \pmod{p^2}$, and $p \ge 3511$.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Write $\ell_2(p)$ for the multiplicative order of $2$ modulo a prime $p$. Let $p$ be an odd prime and $k$ a natural number, and let $F_p(k)$ be the sum of $1/N$ over the integers $N$ with $e^k < N \le e^{k+1}$, $N \equiv p \pmod{p\,\ell_2(p)}$ and $N > p$. Then $F_p(k) \le 2 / (p\,\ell_2(p))$.

results.title: Rankin's bound for reciprocal sums of smooth numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x, y, s$ be real numbers with $2 \le y < x$ and $0 < s < 1$. Call a positive integer $y$-smooth if all its prime factors are at most $y$ (so $1$ is $y$-smooth). Let $S(x, y)$ be the sum of $1/n$ over the $y$-smooth integers $n > x$, and let $\zeta(\sigma, y)$ be the sum of $n^{-\sigma}$ over all $y$-smooth integers $n$. Then $S(x, y) \le x^{-s} \zeta(1 - s, y)$, where both series converge.

results.title: Primes with odd order of 2 of small size
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Write $\ell_2(p)$ for the multiplicative order of $2$ modulo a prime $p$. For every real $x > 0$, the number of primes $p$ with $2 < p \le x$ such that $\ell_2(p)$ is odd and $1 < \ell_2(p) \le p^{2/5}$ is less than $0.00754\, x^{4/5}$.

results.title: Primes with odd order of 2 of medium size
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Write $\ell_2(p)$ for the multiplicative order of $2$ modulo a prime $p$. For every real $x \ge 337$, the number of primes $p$ with $2 < p \le x$ such that $\ell_2(p)$ is odd and $p^{2/5} < \ell_2(p) \le p^{12/25}$ is less than $0.00754\, x^{24/25}$.

results.title: Value of a finite continued fraction
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite list $a_0, a_1, \dots, a_t$ of integers (possibly zero or negative), the value $[a_0; a_1, \dots, a_t]$ is the rational number $a_0 + 1/(a_1 + 1/(\cdots + 1/a_t))$, computed from the right: the empty list has value $0$, and the list $a_0, a_1, \dots, a_t$ has value $a_0 + v^{-1}$, where $v$ is the value of the list $a_1, \dots, a_t$. In particular $[a] = a + 0^{-1} = a$; here and at any vanishing…

results.title: Recursion for finite continued fractions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every integer $a$ and all integers $l_1, \dots, l_n$ with $n \ge 0$, $[a; l_1, \dots, l_n] = a + [l_1; l_2, \dots, l_n]^{-1}$, where the empty continued fraction (the case $n = 0$) has value $0$ and $0^{-1}$ is taken to be $0$ whenever $[l_1; l_2, \dots, l_n] = 0$.

results.title: Continued fraction of length one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every integer $a$, the finite continued fraction $[a]$ has value $a$.

results.title: The continued fraction $(1; 2, 2)$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The finite continued fraction $[1; 2, 2]$ has value $7/5$.

results.title: Folding lemma for finite continued fractions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a_0$ be an integer, let $t$ be even and let $a_1, \dots, a_t$ be integers with $a_i \ge 1$ for every $i$, and let $q$ be the denominator in lowest terms of the value $[a_0; a_1, \dots, a_t]$ of the finite continued fraction. Then for every integer $x \ge 1$, $[a_0; a_1, \dots, a_t] + 1/(x q^2) = [a_0; a_1, \dots, a_t, x, -a_t, \dots, -a_1]$.

results.title: A zero partial quotient merges its neighbours
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all integers $a$ and $b$ and all finite lists of integers $u_1, \dots, u_m$ and $v_1, \dots, v_n$ ($m, n \ge 0$), the finite continued fractions satisfy $[u_1, \dots, u_m, a, 0, b, v_1, \dots, v_n] = [u_1, \dots, u_m, a + b, v_1, \dots, v_n]$.

results.title: Normalizing a negated block
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x \ge 0$ be an integer, let $t \ge 2$ and let $a_1, \dots, a_t$ be integers with $a_i \ge 1$ for every $i$. Then for every finite list of integers $b_1, \dots, b_m$ ($m \ge 0$), the finite continued fractions satisfy $[b_1, \dots, b_m, x, -a_t, -a_{t-1}, \dots, -a_1] = [b_1, \dots, b_m, x - 1, 1, a_t - 1, a_{t-1}, \dots, a_1]$.

results.title: Terms of the paperfolding sums
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a sequence $x = (x_k)_{k \ge 0}$ of natural numbers, the real numbers $s_k$ are defined by $s_0 = 1$ and $s_{k+1} = s_k^2 / x_k$, where the quotient is read as $0$ when $x_k = 0$. They are the terms of the sums $S = \sum_k s_k$.

results.title: First term of the paperfolding sums
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every sequence $x$ of natural numbers, the term $s_0$ of the paperfolding sum terms defined by $x$ equals $1$.

results.title: Recursion for the paperfolding sum terms
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every sequence $x$ of natural numbers and every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the paperfolding sum terms defined by $x$ satisfy $s_{k+1} = s_k^2 / x_k$, where the quotient is read as $0$ when $x_k = 0$.

results.title: Second term of the paperfolding sums
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every sequence $x$ of natural numbers with $x_0 = 2$, the term $s_1$ of the paperfolding sum terms defined by $x$ equals $1/2$.

results.summary: An event `A ⊆ ConfigSpace E` is *increasing* if it is an upper set for the coordinatewise order: `ω ∈ A` and `ω ≤ ω'` imply `ω' ∈ A`. This is `IsUpperSet A`.

results.title: Feedforward network
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: Given layer widths $d : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, a feedforward network with widths $d$ is a sequence of arbitrary maps $f_k : \mathbb{R}^{d(k)} \to \mathbb{R}^{d(k+1)}$, one for each $k \in \mathbb{N}$, where $f_k$ is the map computed by layer $k$ and $\mathbb{R}^n$ carries its Euclidean structure.

results.title: The forward pass
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a feedforward network with layers $f_k : \mathbb{R}^{d_k} \to \mathbb{R}^{d_{k+1}}$ between Euclidean spaces, the forward pass through the first $n$ layers is the map $N_n : \mathbb{R}^{d_0} \to \mathbb{R}^{d_n}$ given by $N_0(x) = x$ and $N_{n+1}(x) = f_n(N_n(x))$, that is, $N_n = f_{n-1} \circ \cdots \circ f_0$.

results.title: The backward pass
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $N$ be a feedforward network with layers $f_k : \mathbb{R}^{d_k} \to \mathbb{R}^{d_{k+1}}$ between Euclidean spaces, let $x \in \mathbb{R}^{d_0}$ be an input, and write $a_k \in \mathbb{R}^{d_k}$ for the forward pass of $x$ through the first $k$ layers. For each $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the backward pass at $x$ sends a vector $\delta \in \mathbb{R}^{d_n}$ to $B_n(\delta) \in \mathbb{R}^{d_0}$, defined by…

results.title: Differentiability along the forward pass
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $N$ be a feedforward network with layers $f_k : \mathbb{R}^{d_k} \to \mathbb{R}^{d_{k+1}}$ between Euclidean spaces, let $x \in \mathbb{R}^{d_0}$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and write $a_j \in \mathbb{R}^{d_j}$ for the forward pass of $x$ through the first $j$ layers. The network is differentiable along the forward pass of $x$ through its first $n$ layers when $f_j$ is differentiable at $a_j$ for every $j < n$.

results.title: Differentiable layers are differentiable along every forward pass
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N$ be a feedforward network with layers $f_k : \mathbb{R}^{d_k} \to \mathbb{R}^{d_{k+1}}$ between Euclidean spaces. If every $f_k$ is differentiable on all of $\mathbb{R}^{d_k}$, then for every input $x \in \mathbb{R}^{d_0}$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the layer $f_j$ is differentiable at the forward pass of $x$ through the first $j$ layers for every $j < n$.

results.title: Differentiability of the forward pass
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N$ be a feedforward network with layers $f_k : \mathbb{R}^{d_k} \to \mathbb{R}^{d_{k+1}}$ between Euclidean spaces, let $x \in \mathbb{R}^{d_0}$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and write $N_j : \mathbb{R}^{d_0} \to \mathbb{R}^{d_j}$ for the forward pass through the first $j$ layers. If $f_j$ is differentiable at $N_j(x)$ for every $j < n$, then $N_n$ is differentiable at $x$.
